topic: What orbital configurations justify prioritizing V-band (57-66 GHz) over optical systems for inter-satellite communication?
consensus_response: V-band (57-66 GHz) systems are prioritized over optical systems due to their resilience to atmospheric disturbances, reduced network overhead, and higher efficiency in managing multi-gateway configurations. V-band systems maintain high performance even in dense weather conditions, offering greater reliability. This resilience, coupled with their ability to achieve higher performance with multi-gateway setups, makes V-band systems more cost-effective and efficient compared to optical systems, which may require more gateways and resources.
reference_context: Optical communications are highly impaired compared to their RF counterparts, but they only need a few gateways to achieve a very high throughput. This directly relates to a reduction in the cost of the ground segment motivating the use of optical communications for feeder links.
